note: Missouri River boat-ramp access on the river side of the levee at the end of gravel Omaha Road. The one designated primitive camping spot is the open mown grass at the edge of the gravel ramp lot, about 30 m from the bank with the river in full view across the lot and ramp lane; there is no pad, shade or facility, and ramp traffic uses the same lot. The ground is unprotected bottomland that floods when the river is high. Spot length is not published. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: MDC 'Individual Campsites' - one mapped Primitive Camping symbol and one GIS point on open grass at the edge of the boat-ramp lot (designated point, so it stays under the lot rule). Free, FCFS, no hookups, 14-day limit. Waterfront: open to the river but the ramp lot lies between - riverview lead (stored riverfront). Pin fine. Phone matches.
flags: INCLUSION (lot rule - stays on a designated point, but it is thin): the area page lists 'Camping: Individual Campsites' and says only 'This area provides access to the Missouri River' (2.7 acres). The 3/09 map draws one Primitive Camping Area symbol inside the road loop just north-west of the Parking Lot square, and GIS layer 27 has one 'Primitive Camping Area' point (OBJECTID 264) 15 m from the lot centre, at the lot's north-east edge. On the 0.24 m/px frame the loop the map draws is now a single gravel lot/turnaround about 40 x 35 m with the concrete ramp running east from its south-east corner; the ground around it is open mown grass, with no pad, table, fire ring or privy visible. So the designated spot is the grass margin of the ramp lot - it passes the rule as written (a mapped symbol and a GIS point at the lot edge, as Lick Creek), but there is nothing here beyond a ramp lot. Owner's call if that is too thin. A 23-ft rig fits (level gravel lot, gravel road, no ford; the road crosses the levee on the way in).

WATERFRONT (stored riverfront) - DOWNGRADE LEAD to riverview: the camping point is ~30 m from the water's edge and the view is fully open - no levee (the map draws the levee ~250 m north, at the area entrance) and no timber between; the only trees are a short line on the bank 50 m east. But what lies between the point and the bank is the gravel ramp lot and the ramp lane, i.e. a driveway and day use, which by the 2026-11-01 rulings blocks on-water. The map's symbol position (inside the old loop) is ~60 m from the bank with the whole lot between. There is no strip of open grass between a camping spot and the river that is not the lot. So: riverview, not riverfront. apply.py does not write waterfront; flagged.
PIN: stored 39.90801,-95.16163 = GIS point 264 at the lot's north-east edge - fine.
PHONE: (816) 271-3100 on the area page matches.

Season (manual, year-round) left as stored; no brochure is published for this area. The site is riverward of the levee, so it will be under water in a Missouri River flood - nothing on the page says so; caveat in the note is from the map and imagery.
